# Test fixtures

Known inputs for software checks and exploratory comparisons. Keep image inputs
in `images/`; future file types can have their own directories here. A fixture is
a documented test input, rather than an arbitrary user upload or generated result.

All current images are **synthetic**, generated by Gazoken. No camera photographs,
private research data, or third-party images are included. This small set is not
a representative forensic benchmark and establishes no detector accuracy.

The [`jpeg-inspector/`](jpeg-inspector/README.md) subdirectory adds tiny structural
JPEG cases with fictitious EXIF, progressive scans, truncation, and appended data.

## Image cases

Every input is 768 × 512 pixels. Open the workbench and choose a file from
`tests/fixtures/images/`.

| File | Construction and what to explore |
| --- | --- |
| [01-reference.png](images/01-reference.png) | Baseline signal chart: seeded texture/noise, a smooth gradient, shapes, and edges. Compare normal scene variation in the residual and Sobel views. |
| [02-reference-q90.jpg](images/02-reference-q90.jpg) | JPEG encoding of the reference at quality 90. A benign control for ELA; compression differences do not establish content editing. |
| [03-recompressed-q55.jpg](images/03-recompressed-q55.jpg) | The quality-90 JPEG decoded and recompressed at quality 55 with chroma subsampling. Ordinary processing only; useful for comparing compression effects. |
| [04-local-smoothing.png](images/04-local-smoothing.png) | A known rectangular region of the reference blurred with Gaussian radius 4. Compare fine detail inside and outside that region. |
| [05-local-smoothing-q90.jpg](images/05-local-smoothing-q90.jpg) | The smoothed image encoded at JPEG quality 90. Compare with the baseline JPEG; ELA need not highlight the edited region. |
| [06-copy-move.png](images/06-copy-move.png) | A 112 × 112 textured patch containing a circle copied into the gradient region. The workbench does not yet implement a copy-move detector. |
| [07-red-lsb-control.png](images/07-red-lsb-control.png) | Reference with red bit 0 cleared everywhere. Red channel / bit 0 should be black. |
| [08-red-lsb-pattern.png](images/08-red-lsb-pattern.png) | Same control with a border and the word GAZOKEN placed in red bit 0. Select Red / bit 0 to see the exact binary pattern. Other channel bits are unchanged. |

ELA is deliberately disabled for PNG inputs. Use the JPEG cases to exercise ELA.
The bit-plane pair demonstrates a known one-bit pattern, not a general-purpose
steganography scheme or a method for extracting unknown messages.

## Ground truth and provenance

`images/masks/` contains three grayscale masks:

- `smooth-patch.png`: selected region for the blur operation.
- `copy-move-target.png`: destination rectangle of the pasted patch.
- `red-lsb-pattern.png`: exact pattern written into red bit 0.

White marks the constructed region or pattern; black marks everything else.
A blur-region mask does not assert that every enclosed pixel changed. JPEG
encoding can introduce differences outside a local edit mask. These masks are
construction records, not predicted detector outputs.

[manifest.json](manifest.json) records parent inputs, operations, coordinates,
seed, dimensions, generator environment, file sizes, and SHA-256 checksums.
Coordinates start at the upper-left, with half-open boxes `(x0, y0, x1, y1)`.

## Regeneration

From the repository root, using Python with Pillow installed:

```bash
python3 tests/generate_fixtures.py
```

The generator overwrites its named fixtures and manifest. The initial set was
created with Python 3.12 and Pillow 10.2.0; exact runtime versions and the JPEG
codec version are recorded in the manifest. Fixed seeds make the construction
repeatable, but codec or Pillow changes can alter encoded bytes. Check the
manifest and review differences when regenerating with another environment.

Keep future inputs small, attributable, and documented. Store large or restricted
research datasets elsewhere and track their manifests in the appropriate
repository. Save analysis outputs separately from these reference inputs.

## User-facing gallery

`assets/samples.json` selects five of these existing files with concise exploration
notes. The static pixel workbench offers all five; the JPEG inspector and local
Python workbench offer the three JPEG cases. The PNG bit-plane pair must remain
lossless. Samples illustrate measurements and controlled constructions, not
validated detection performance. No new image data was generated for this gallery.
